instruction: How do I set up Tailwind CSS?
output: Install the CLI (`npm i -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/cli`) with `@import "tailwindcss";` in your CSS, or the classic config route (`tailwindcss init`, content paths, directives). The engine scans source files and generates only used utilities — production CSS stays kilobytes, not megabytes.

instruction: What is utility-first CSS in Tailwind?
output:
```html
<button class="rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-4 py-2 font-bold text-white hover:bg-blue-700">Simpan</button>
```
Style by composing small utilities in markup instead of naming custom classes. Reads verbose at first, but eliminates dead CSS, naming debates and specificity wars — the stylesheet is generated from what you actually use.

instruction: How do I do dark mode in Tailwind?
output: Use class strategy (`darkMode: "class"` in v3; v4 `custom-variant dark`) so a `.dark` ancestor toggles: `<div class="bg-white text-black dark:bg-black dark:text-white">`. Pair with the app's theme store + `prefers-color-scheme` default. Never ship dark: variants without a toggle — half your users get the wrong theme.

When should I use @apply in Tailwind?
output:
```css
.btn-utama { @apply rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-4 py-2 text-white; }
```
Use @apply for genuinely repeated component patterns to cut markup noise — but overuse recreates the custom-CSS problems Tailwind removes (dead code, specificity). Rule: three repetitions of identical utility chains earns an @apply or a framework component.

instruction: Why is my Tailwind production CSS huge?
output: The `content` paths miss your templates, so nothing purges — set them to cover every file with classes (`./src/**/*.{html,js,ts,jsx,tsx}`). Dev builds look big (JIT in memory); production `build` output should be tens of KB. If still large, grep for dynamic class construction (`bg-${color}`) which the scanner cannot see — safelist those.
